participants: Angelo DiMaggio (running the meeting, deputising for Chris)
Kim Forbes-Sobers (setter, UK — referred to throughout as 'he'/'bro')
summary: Regular sales team meeting run by Angelo DiMaggio standing in for Chris, covering wins, weekly projections and the rollout of a new end-of-day reporting platform called Piff Perfect that replaces the existing Google Sheet. Angelo walked the team through the new metric definitions — in particular the distinction between show rate and 'slot show rate' — and screen-shared Harry Edmonds' individual month-to-date numbers, live, including deal counts, cash collected and revenue. Pipeline projections were reviewed by name, with Harry forecasting a $6,000 pay-in-full and a $1,200 payment this week and Kim reporting on set and show-rate targets. The meeting also covered Kim's new, more aggressive price pre-framing on setter calls, and Angelo confirmed that a former closer, Vince, is now handling renewal sales.
notable: PAYMENT PLAN TERMS STATED AS POLICY: Angelo defined the standard instalment plan while teaching data entry — 'let's say somebody signed up on a six pay and the six pay is six payments of 1,200. The revenue would be 7,200.' That is $7,200 on instalments against a $6,000 cash price, a $1,200 premium, and the structure was never described in those terms to any prospect in this batch.

THREE PRICE TIERS ARE OFFICIAL, NOT TWO: the reporting platform tracks 3-month, 6-month and 12-month units — 'we have three different tiers or programs' and 'You sold 12M, 12-month programs, 12 6Ms, and then 0 3Ms.' This corroborates the $4,000 three-month tier quoted on the Ross Surratt call and means the $6,000/6mo plus $9,000/12mo structure is not the full commercial menu.

THE $1,200 ON THE FREDERICK EISLER CALL IS EXPLAINED HERE: Harry reported the same prospect by name — 'Probably Frederick will close, Kim, this weekend. Probably be a love-it-or-leave-it, though, because he didn't want to get scammed. He was like, I'm a 67-year-old, and I keep hearing about people getting scammed. I was like, dude, just do a month.' He then forecast 'heavily likely to have a 1200 this week too.' Internally it is a first instalment; the prospect was told it was a down payment with the balance settled later.

THE COMPANY'S OWN HISTORICAL METRICS ARE ACKNOWLEDGED AS UNRELIABLE: 'Harry, when I was like doing your numbers, I noticed some of your numbers like didn't actually make sense... your scheduled calls wasn't actually like accurate', and 'some of it's not going to like look completely accurate is because we weren't tracking some of these numbers on the previous spreadsheet... some of it may have gotten brought over from April. Really, some of these numbers are only going to be accurate if you look from May on.'

HARRY'S MONTH-TO-DATE NUMBERS, READ OUT LIVE: 117 slots available, 98 slots booked, 133 scheduled calls, 52 live calls, 37 offers, 12 deals, 4 deposits; show rate 39%, slot show rate 53%, call-to-close 23%, offer-to-close 32%; $36K cash collected against $78K revenue generated. Note 52 live calls against only 37 offers — fifteen live calls where no offer was made, which matches the two calls in this batch that ended without a price being quoted.
PRIOR-DAY NUMBERS: 7 slots available, 6 booked, 7 scheduled calls, 2 live calls, 1 offer, 0 deals, 0 deposits — a 28.5% show rate and 33% slot show rate.

REP SELF-REPORTS A TWO-WEEK PERFORMANCE COLLAPSE COVERING THIS BATCH: 'I think I had 50% close rate first week. And then the last two weeks it's like, that's when the wounds have been opened', and 'This week's just been a bad week in terms of my sales ability. It's like the week I've had the highest show rate and the worst close rate.' The calls in this batch fall inside that window.

MANDATED 1-1s DESCRIBED AS TRAUMA WORK: 'I'm doing one-on-ones with Brian, and obviously it's not really sales training, it's like opening childhood trauma wounds... the last thing that's on my mind is like handling a wife objection when it comes up.' The response was a single question and an immediate subject change to haircuts.

SETTER PRICE PRE-FRAMING IS A NEW, DELIBERATE POLICY: Kim on 'the new process of, like, disqualifying a tad more' — 'saying it will be in the few, like, a few thousands, has been landing really well', and his handling of the $200/month expectation: 'is that just what you had in mind? Or is that more so just because that's all you could afford right now'. Angelo coached the follow-up: 'you can definitely get $200 a month stuff. But it's not going to be really the level of one-on-one, hands-on coaching expertise that Trevor's going to give you.'
TARGETS: Angelo set Harry a goal of 'another 11K this week and get you to 50, and upfront cash by the end of next week'; Kim's weekly unit target is eight, which he expected to miss.

PERSONNEL: Kyla (setter code KL) confirmed as a team member; Kim Forbes-Sobers (KFS) confirmed as male and hired around October from a Trevor Instagram post; Andrew Musial is based in Poland; 'Farouk' referenced as another closer taking slots; Vince is a former closer now working renewal sales — 'he's mainly helping out with renewal sales' — meaning a renewals motion exists outside this corpus entirely.

TOOLING: end-of-day reporting moves from a Google Sheet to Piff Perfect (piffperfect.com) effective this date, with a Google form retained for qualitative call summaries. Angelo has admin access to and has been entering data inside individual reps' accounts: 'Harry, I've been actually in your account... Kim, same, same with you.'
CLIENT DESCRIBED BY NATIONALITY AND ACCENT AS A 'WIN': Harry's reported win was 'Closed in Indian, with an Indian accent', followed by Andrew's 'And he did a bargain.'
